children: The Centre is examining the implications of airport operators owning airlines and vice versa, and will take a balanced approach, Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Tuesday.

Speaking on the sidelines of an event, the Minister said no decision had been taken yet and the matter remained under deliberation. He was responding to a question on the Adani Group’s interest in starting an airline.
At present, the Adani Group operates several airports under the public-private partnership model.
While the government wants more airlines to enter the market and provide passengers with greater choice, the Minister said common ownership of airports and airlines requires closer examination.
“However, airports and airlines operating together require deliberation. We will examine the pros and cons and take a balanced approach,” he said.
According to Naidu, the government supports interest in establishing new airlines. However, an airport operator’s entry into airline operations raises issues that would need to be addressed.
“But when an airport operator wants to operate an airline, we also have to examine the potential disadvantages. We need to create a system that addresses those concerns,” he said.
When asked if a decision on the issue had been taken, Naidu said: “No decision yet.”

Besides, the Minister said there was no general government rule preventing airport operators from owning airlines, apart from provisions in the Operation, Management and Development Agreements (OMDAs) for Delhi and Mumbai airports.
“As such, there is no clause or rule in the government that prevents airport operators from owning airlines, other than the OMDA agreements for Delhi and Mumbai,” he said.
Furthermore, he did not elaborate on the specific agreement provisions or the changes that could be considered.

title: Centre to take a call on airport-airline cross ownership
